rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī directs readers to his earlier discussion of guidance in 6:125.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في تفسير قوله فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام الأنعام 125

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse sums up the preceding account of guidance while also explaining the guidance provided by the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: كالإجمال بعد التفصيل بالنسبة إلى الآية السابقة بالنظر إلى ما يتحصل من الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The best discourse” is the Qur’an; ḥadīth here means speech, as in 52:34 and 77:50.
rows.anchor: والحديث هو القول كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is the best speech because it contains pure truth, untouched by falsehood, and is God’s majestic speech.
rows.anchor: فهو أحسن القول لاشتماله على محض الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “mutashābih” means that the Qur’an’s parts resemble one another; unlike ambiguous verses, this quality belongs to the whole book.
rows.anchor: يشبه بعض أجزائه بعضا وهذا غير التشابه الذي في المتشابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathānī is the plural of mathniya, something turned back: Qur’anic verses refer back to, clarify, and interpret one another.
rows.anchor: جمع مثنية بمعنى المعطوف لانعطاف بعض آياته على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses explain one another without contradiction, as affirmed by 4:82.
rows.anchor: من غير اختلاف فيها بحيث يدفع بعضه بعضا ويناقضه

words: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause describing the skin’s shudder is an adjective of the book, not a new independent sentence.
rows.anchor: والاقشعرار تقبض الجلد تقبضا شديدا

words: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqshiʿrār is a strong contraction of the skin caused by fear on hearing or seeing something awe-inspiring.
rows.anchor: والاقشعرار تقبض الجلد تقبضا شديدا لخشية عارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear God understand their own position before His majesty; hearing His speech turns them toward divine greatness, bringing fear to their hearts and a shudder to their skin.
rows.anchor: لأنهم على تبصر من موقف نفوسهم قبال عظمة ربهم

words: ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talīnu carries the sense of settling and becoming tranquil, which explains its construction with ilā: their skin and hearts rest in and accept God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: مضمنة معنى السكون والطمأنينة ولذا عدي بالى

words: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts are not mentioned with the shudder because “hearts” means souls, which experience fear but do not physically shudder.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر القلوب في الجملة السابقة عند ذكر الاقشعرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is God’s guidance” refers to the sequence of Qur’anic awe and then the settling of skin and hearts into remembrance, defining guidance by its effect.
rows.anchor: أي ما يأخذهم من اقشعرار الجلود من القرآن ثم سكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides through this guidance servants whose readiness remains intact and who are not obstructed by wrongdoing or sin.
rows.anchor: يهدي بهداه من يشاء من عباده وهو الذي لم يبطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording suggests that guidance is bestowed by grace, not imposed as something to which God is compelled.
rows.anchor: وفي السياق إشعار بأن الهداية من فضله وليس بموجب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes “that” to refer to the Qur’an; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل المشار إليه بقوله { ذلك هدى الله } القرآن وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer that guidance is exclusively God’s act, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the verse does not establish that.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بالآيات على أن الهداية من صنع الله لا يشاركه فيها غيره

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance belongs to God directly or through guides He has guided; whoever He leaves unguided in both ways has no guide.
rows.anchor: فالهداية كلها لله إما بلا واسطة أو بواسطة الهداة المهديين من خلقه وعلى هذا

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement is repeated elsewhere in God’s speech.
rows.anchor: فلا هادي له وذلك قوله في ذيل الآية { ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد } وسيأتي الجملة بعد عدة آيات وهي متكررة في كلامه تعالى

words: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse contrasts the people of punishment with those secure from it, representing the misguided and the guided and continuing the previous verse.
rows.anchor: مقايسة بين أهل العذاب يوم القيامة والآمنين منه

words: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is rejecting; the predicate after “whoever” is omitted, understood as “like one who is safe from it.”
rows.anchor: محذوف والتقدير كمن هو في أمن منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī construes “on the Day of Resurrection” as modifying “guards himself.”
rows.anchor: ويوم القيامة متعلق بيتقي، والمعنى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the person shields himself with his face because his hand, normally used to ward off harm, is shackled to his neck.
rows.anchor: كذا قيل. وقيل الاتقاء بوجهه بالمعنى المذكور

words: يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī objects that the face is not a means of shielding oneself; an alternative reading makes the phrase refer to warding off future punishment through piety, but he finds it forced.
rows.anchor: وقيل الاتقاء بوجهه بالمعنى المذكور لا وجه له

words: وقيل للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers telling the wrongdoers to taste the result of their deeds are the angels of the Fire; the clause may include an implied qad or not.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الجملة بتقدير قد أو بدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them “the wrongdoers” instead of using a pronoun identifies their wrongdoing as the cause of the sentence.
rows.anchor: لكن وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير للدلالة على علة الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier rejecters were struck from an unexpected direction, taken by surprise; such a sudden seizure is especially severe.
rows.anchor: أي من الجهة التي لا يحتسبون ففوجؤا وأخذوا على غفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses recount humiliating punishment suffered by some disbelievers as a warning to others.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية وما بعدها بيان لما أصاب بعض الكفار من عذاب الخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khizy means humiliation and abasement; God made earlier peoples taste it through drowning, sinking, blasts, earthquakes, transformation, and killing.
rows.anchor: الخزي هو الذل والصغار، وقد أذاقهم الله ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives people examples of every kind so they may awaken, reflect, and take admonition from their meanings.
rows.anchor: أي ضربنا لهم من كل نوع من الأمثال شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAwaj means deviation or bending.
rows.anchor: العوج الانحراف والانعطاف، { قرآنا عربيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “An Arabic Qur’an” is accusative either as praise with an implied verb such as “I praise,” or as a circumstantial accusative relying on the description.
rows.anchor: منصوب على المدح بتقدير أمدح أو أخص ونحوه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says shaks, with fatḥa then kasra, means ill-tempered; the partners are quarrelsome because of their bad temper.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الشكس - بالفتح فالكسر - سيء الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners are contentious with one another because of their disagreeable dispositions.
rows.anchor: أي متشاجرون لشكاسة خلقهم. انتهى وفسروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators explain salaman as something purely belonging to one person, not shared among many.
rows.anchor: وفسروا السلم بالخالص الذي لا يشترك فيه كثيرون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view takes “worst” and “best” as absolute superlatives, since all disobedience is worst and all obedience best.
rows.anchor: وقيل صيغة التفضيل في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the highest degree of their deeds may determine their raised rank, preserving the final perfection their deeds reached, though applying a parallel formulation to covering the worst is unclear.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال إن المراد أنه ينظر إلى أرفع أعمالهم درجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those besides Him” refers to the polytheists’ gods, while “His servant” refers to the one praised in the preceding verses, primarily the Prophet.
rows.anchor: المراد بالذين من دونه آلهتهم من دون الله على ما يستفاد من السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question seeks affirmation: God is sufficient for His servants, reassuring the Prophet against threats involving their idols and implicitly promising protection.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام للتقرير والمعنى هو يكفيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implicit promise of sufficiency is stated explicitly in 2:137.
rows.anchor: كما صرح به في قوله فسيكفيكهم الله وهو السميع العليم البقرة 137

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two reciprocal statements are universal maxims; naming God rather than using a pronoun is an apparent noun in place of a pronoun.
rows.anchor: جملتان كالمتعاكستين مرسلتان إرسال الضوابط الكلية

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their placement after the promise of sufficiency signals that the idol-threateners will not find guidance or attain their aims against the Prophet, whom God has guided.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن هؤلاء المخوفين لا يهتدون بالإيمان أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s might and retributive power explain the maxims: He punishes those who deny truth and persist in unbelief, and no one can overcome Him or mislead a servant He guides.
rows.anchor: فإن عزته وكونه ذا انتقام يقتضيان أن ينتقم ممن

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation implies that divine misguidance is retribution and punishment, not an initial act of leading someone astray.
rows.anchor: وفي التعليل دلالة على أن الإضلال المنسوب إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that when divine light enters the heart it expands; its signs are detachment from worldly delusion, turning toward the eternal abode, and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr transmits the report through Ibn Mardawayh from Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī from Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn Jarīr and others from Qatāda.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الدر المنثور عن ابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī’s tafsir says this verse was revealed about ʿAlī; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī objects that the whole sūra’s one-time revelation does not fit that report.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that people asked the Prophet to tell them stories, after which the verse describing the Qur’an as the best discourse was revealed; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls this an application of the verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قالوا يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا فنزل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when a servant’s skin shudders from fear of God, sins fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
rows.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Anas attributes to the Prophet the interpretation “uncreated”; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the verse does not fit this report.
rows.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers readers to his earlier discussion of divine speech at the end of 2:253.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم كلام في معنى الكلام في ذيل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Al-Ḥākim al-Haskānī transmits from ʿAlī that he is the man wholly belonging to the Messenger; a parallel report comes through al-ʿAyyāshī from Abū Khālid from Abū Jaʿfar.
rows.anchor: بالإسناد عن علي أنه قال أنا ذلك الرجل السلم لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The identification of ʿAlī is an application of the example, whose meaning remains general.
rows.anchor: وهو من الجري والمثل عام

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says they initially thought the dispute verse concerned Muslims and the People of the Book, then recognized it concerned them after seeing Muslims fight one another with swords.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر كنا نرى أن هذه فينا وفي أهل الكتابين

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says the Muslims recognized the dispute in the verse when they fought one another at Ṣiffīn.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري كنا نقول إن ربنا واحد ونبينا واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr transmits the first report through several routes and from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, and similar reports from al-Zubayr; the second comes through Saʿīd b. Manṣūr.
rows.anchor: وروى الحديث الثاني عن سعيد بن منصور عن أبي سعيد الخدري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports conflict with the claim that the Companions are rewarded as juristic interpreters whether they are right or wrong.
rows.anchor: والأحاديث تعارض ما روي أن الصحابة مجتهدون مأجورون

rows.speaker: أئمة الهدى من آل محمد
rows.claim: A view identified with the Imams of the Prophet’s family says Muhammad brought the truth and ʿAlī affirmed it; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī treats it as an application of the verse.
rows.anchor: وصدق به علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام وهو المروي عن أئمة الهدى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr also transmits the Muhammad-and-ʿAlī interpretation through Ibn Mardawayh from Abū Hurayra.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الدر المنثور عن ابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the Muhammad-and-ʿAlī identification an application, noting that the verse ends by describing the subjects as God-fearing.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه من الجري نظرا إلى قوله في ذيل الآية

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Another transmitted application identifies Abū Bakr as the one who affirmed the truth.
rows.anchor: وروي من طرقهم أن الذي صدق به أبو بكر

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Another application says Gabriel brought the truth and Muhammad affirmed it; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it because the passage describes the Prophet and believers, while Gabriel is unrelated to its context.
rows.anchor: روي أن الذي جاء به جبريل والذي صدق به محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding discussion points to hidden delights prepared for the righteous, as stated in 32:17.
rows.anchor: فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين السجدة 17

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “appearing” mentioned in the context is disclosure after concealment, as in 50:22.
rows.anchor: مقتضى السياق أن البدو المذكور من قبيل الظهور بعد الخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their evil deeds become manifest after having been hidden from them, as in 3:30.
rows.anchor: أي ظهر لهم سيئات أعمالهم بعد ما كانت خفية عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What surrounds them is the terrors, hardships, and kinds of punishment of Resurrection that religious authorities warned about and they mocked in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ونزل عليهم وأصابهم ما كانوا يستهزؤون به في الدنيا إذا سمعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains the preceding description of wrongdoers; its opening faʾ links the explanation to what came before.
rows.anchor: الآية في مقام التعليل البياني لما تقدم من وصف الظالمين

words: فإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعانا ثم إذا خولناه نعمة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature follows desire and is deluded by worldly blessings and visible means: in hardship people turn sincerely to God, but after relief they credit their own skill and forget that bounty is a test.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان حليف النسيان إذا مسه الضر أقبل إلى ربه وأخلص له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍurr here means illness or hardship.
rows.anchor: أي مرض أو شدة { دعانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls upon God alone in supplication and cuts himself off from others.
rows.anchor: أي خصنا بالدعاء وانقطع عن غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwalah means to give as a gift; “a bounty from Us” marks it as an actual bounty.
rows.anchor: التخويل الإعطاء على نحو الهبة، وتقييد النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “I was given it” refers to the bounty as a thing or property, reflecting the speaker’s refusal to acknowledge it as a gift from God.
rows.anchor: للنعمة بما أنه شيء أو مال والعناية في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By calling it a bounty “from Us” and then saying merely “I was given it,” the Qur’an captures the speaker’s detachment of the benefit from its giver.
rows.anchor: فيسميها شيئا أو مالا ونحوه ولا يسميها نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, the speaker means “through my own knowledge”: his expertise in earning a living, acquiring wealth, and accumulating money.
rows.anchor: والملائم لسياق الآية أن يكون معنى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the speaker received the bounty because God knew he was good and deserved it; another says he knew God was pleased with him.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد إنما أوتيته على علم من الله بخير عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects both alternatives because they do not fit the preceding explanation of the statement.
rows.anchor: وأنت خبير بأن ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bounty God gives is a trial and examination, though most people do not know this.
rows.anchor: أي بل النعمة التي خولناه منا فتنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternative readings say the bounty itself is a punishment, or that the boastful statement is a trial for which its speaker is punished; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī finds both far-fetched, especially the latter.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه بل تلك النعمة عذاب لهم، وقيل المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “they said it” returns to the preceding statement, treating it as a saying or utterance.
rows.anchor: راجع إلى القول السابق باعتبار أنه مقالة أو كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the boast by showing that if people earned bounty by their own power, their effort would preserve it and benefit them, yet their predecessors’ deeds did not save them from ruin.
rows.anchor: والآية رد لقولهم وإثبات لكونها فتنة يمتحنون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predecessors who made this boast likely include Qarun, whose story in 28:78 records the same claim.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الآية تشير بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “These” refers to the Prophet’s people; their punishment and inability to escape God will match that of earlier wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بهؤلاء إلى قومه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a second answer to the claim that wealth comes from personal knowledge; the first answer used the predecessors as a reductio, while this one counters it with evidence.
rows.anchor: جواب آخر عن قول القائل منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human effort and knowledge are not sufficient causes of provision, since many seekers return disappointed and many efforts fail.
rows.anchor: أن سعي الإنسان عن علم وإرادة لتحصيل الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision depends on innumerable external causes, conditions, and impediments across time and place; their convergence is not mere chance, since chance is neither constant nor predominant.
rows.anchor: فهناك علل وشرائط زمانية ومكانية وموانع مختلفة باختلاف الظروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stable, vast order governing provision for living beings extends throughout the world; without it, things would perish immediately.
rows.anchor: وقانون ارتزاق المرتزقين الشامل للموجودات الحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion distinguishes true visions of the greater imaginal realm from satanic fantasies arising in the lesser imaginal realm, which have no interpretation.
rows.anchor: فمهما رأت في ملكوت السماوات فهو مما له تأويل

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī explains to ʿUmar that God takes all souls in sleep and death: visions seen while souls are with God in heaven are true, while devils fabricate falsehoods when souls return to their bodies.
rows.anchor: فقال علي بن أبي طالب أفلا أخبرك بذلك يا أمير المؤمنين

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar marvels that some dreams prove exactly true while others amount to nothing; the report is transmitted from Sulaym b. ʿĀmir through Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.
rows.anchor: عن سليم بن عامر أن عمر بن الخطاب قال العجب من رؤيا الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī directs readers to his fuller treatment of dreams in Sūrat Yūsuf and interprets “heaven” and “between heaven and earth” as the greater and lesser imaginal worlds.
rows.anchor: أقول تقدم تفصيل الكلام في الرؤيا في سورة يوسف والرجوع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The earth” includes the earth itself, its contents, and what is connected to it, as in the earlier phrase that the earth is wholly in God’s grasp.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأرض مع ذلك للأرض وما فيها وما يتعلق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many passages support the manifestation and embodiment of deeds and the testimony of bodily members, including 50:22, 3:30, and 99:4–8.
rows.anchor: وآيات أخرى كثيرة تدل على ظهور الأعمال وتجسمها وشهادة الأعضاء وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes “the Book” to mean the reckoning; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses this as obvious.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد به الحساب وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the Book as the records of deeds by which people are judged and sentenced.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به صحائف الأعمال التي يحاسب عليها ويقضى بها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third view identifies the Book with the Preserved Tablet, supported by 45:29.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به اللوح المحفوظ ويؤيده قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets are asked whether they conveyed their messages, as in 7:6.
rows.anchor: أما النبيون فليسألوا عن أداء رسالتهم كما يشعر به السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses are witnesses of deeds, brought forward to give testimony to what they observed, as in 4:41.
rows.anchor: وأما الشهداء وهم شهداء الأعمال فليؤدوا ما تحملوه من الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun refers to people understood from context; the judgment concerns their disputes and disagreements, as in 45:17.
rows.anchor: والقضاء بينهم هو القضاء فيما اختلفوا فيه الوارد كرارا في كلامه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawfiyah means giving in full; the verse says each soul receives what it did, rather than naming its recompense, precluding doubt about the judgment’s justice.
rows.anchor: التوفية الإعطاء بالتمام وقد علقت بنفس ما عملت دون جزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The records, prophets, and witnesses are not needed because God lacks knowledge; they make the judgment proceed according to equity and justice.
rows.anchor: ليس حكمه بهذا النمط من وضع الكتاب والمجيء بالنبيين والشهداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verse describes the judgment, this verse its execution, and the following verses detail that execution.
rows.anchor: والآية السابقة تتضمن القضاء والحكم وهذه الآية إجراؤه

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines sawq as urging someone onward to travel.
rows.anchor: السوق بالفتح فالسكون - على ما في المجمع - الحث على السير

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines zumar as groups of people.
rows.anchor: والزمر جمع زمرة وهي - كما في الصحاح - الجماعة من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are urged toward Hell in successive groups; when they reach it, its seven gates are opened for their entry.
rows.anchor: والمعنى { وسيق } وحث على السير { الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا } جماعة بعد جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage admonishes its audience to inspect earlier peoples’ traces and stories, learn from them, and recognize that God defeats power, arrogance, and plotting; Moses and Pharaoh’s believer are examples.
rows.anchor: بيان في الآيات موعظتهم بالإرجاع إلى آثار الأمم الماضين وقصصهم للنظر والاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is rejecting; the addressed people should travel and look reflectively at what happened to earlier nations that denied their messengers.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أو لم يسيروا هؤلاء الذين أرسلناك إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier rejecters had greater power, capacity, and authority than the present audience.
rows.anchor: كانوا هم أشد منهم قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their āthār were monumental traces such as fortified cities, impregnable citadels, and tall, solidly built palaces.
rows.anchor: كالمدائن الحصينة والقلاع المنيعة والقصور العالية المشيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seized and destroyed them because of their deeds, and they had no protector to shield them from Him.
rows.anchor: فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم } وأهلكهم بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāqin is an active participle meaning one who protects or preserves.
rows.anchor: وما كان لهم من الله من واق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the divine seizure; bayyināt are clear signs, and the rest is straightforward.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالبينات الآيات الواضحات، والباقي ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs may be miracles such as the staff and hand; the manifest authority may be God’s overpowering support that kept Pharaoh from killing Moses and extinguishing his light.
rows.anchor: لعل المراد بالآيات الخوارق المعجزة التي أرسل بها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the signs as proofs and arguments, and the manifest authority as Moses’ miracles such as the staff and hand; the source notes other views too.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالآيات الحجج والدلالات وبالسلطان معجزاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh was the Copts’ tyrant and king, Haman his minister, and Qarun a tyrant among the Israelites with abundant treasure.
rows.anchor: وهامان وزيره وقارون من طغاة بني إسرائيل ذو الخزائن المليئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three alone are named because they were the principal roots of corruption and turmoil among both peoples.
rows.anchor: وإنما اختص الثلاثة من بين الأمتين بالذكر لكونهم اصولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses brought truth from God, which deserved acceptance, but his opponents answered with a plot to prevent anyone from believing; God nullified their scheme.
rows.anchor: فقد جاءهم بالحق وكان من الواجب أن يقبلوه لأنه حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context suggests Qarun joined the call to kill the boys, despite being an Israelite, because the decree first applied to Israelites generally and he may have opposed Moses and his followers.
rows.anchor: ويشعر السياق أن من القائلين بهذا القول قارون وهو من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “believed with him” rather than “believed in him” signals that the believers supported Moses in his mission.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل آمنوا به إشارة إلى مظاهرتهم موسى في دعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dharūnī means “leave me alone”; Pharaoh addresses his council.
rows.anchor: أي اتركوني، خطاب يخاطب به ملأه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s words suggest that people around him were advising him not to kill Moses and to desist from harming him.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أنه كان هناك قوم يشيرون عليه أن لا يقتل موسى
